hypothesis: On K = -k^2 the Jacobi fields grow like e^(kL), so absolute errors are amplified by e^(kL) and a fixed relative accuracy needs steps growing with k; this is intrinsic instability of the flow (eigenvalues +k and -k of the Jacobi linearization), not classical stiffness, so A-stable implicit methods do not remove it. Concentrated negative curvature (Saddle with large c) does not produce exponential growth. On the full nonlinear systems a Gauss-Legendre integrator keeps its constant-curvature advantage only for the Jacobi field on constant K, and its symmetry keeps the speed error bounded where RK4's drifts only on recurrent geodesics.
input_data: HyperbolicPlane(k), k in 1, 2, 4, 8, start (0, 1), heading 0.6, L = 2.0
RK4 N = 128; DP45 rtol 1e-10; relative accuracy target 1e-06; implicit midpoint and 2-stage Gauss-Legendre as exact step matrices
Saddle(c), c in 1, 4, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096, 16384, ridge geodesic y = 0 from arclength 1 before the saddle point, L = 2, DP45 rtol 1e-9 (checked at 1e-11)

Full nonlinear systems: 2-stage Gauss-Legendre (fixed-point stage solve to 1e-13, at most 60 iterations) and RK4 on HyperbolicPlane(k) with N = 64, 128, 256; on Saddle(c), c in 1, 4, 16, the ridge geodesic and an oblique one from (x0, 0.5/c) with heading -0.3, N = 32, 64, 128; 32, 64, 128; 64, 128, 256, against DP45 at rtol 1e-13 (checked at 1e-12)

Speed drift at h = 0.25 for RK4, implicit midpoint and Gauss-Legendre: HyperbolicPlane(1) from (0, 1) heading 0.6 and the oblique Saddle(1) geodesic to L = 32; Torus(2, 1) from (0, 0) heading 1.3 (winds around the tube) to L = 160
mathematical_model: j'' = k^2 j, j_head = sinh(kL)/k. A one-step method of order p with R(z) = e^z (1 + c z^(p+1) + ...) on the growing mode has relative error N |c| (kh)^(p+1), so N(tau) = L (L |c| k^(p+1) / tau)^(1/p) ~ k^((p+1)/p): RK4 c = -1/120 (k^(5/4)), implicit midpoint c = 1/12 (k^(3/2), pole at kh = 2 and negative factor beyond), 2-stage Gauss-Legendre (the (2, 2) Pade approximant) c = -1/720 (k^(5/4), no real pole). RK4 stability for the decaying mode needs kh <= 2.785. Saddle ridge y = 0: K = -c^2/(1 + c^2 x^2)^2 ~ -1/(4 s^2) away from the saddle point, where j'' = j/(4 s^2) has solutions |s|^((1 +/- sqrt(2))/2); matching the inbound and outbound power laws through the core of width 1/c gives j_head(L) ~ c^sqrt(2) (matched asymptotics, not a proof). The nonlinear Gauss-Legendre integrator is the same collocation method, so on constant K its Jacobi columns equal the step-matrix powers up to the stage-solve tolerance; the geodesic equation is nonlinear, where the linear error constants say nothing. Gauss methods are symmetric (applied in chart position-velocity coordinates they are not symplectic for the geodesic Hamiltonian), so on a reversible integrable problem with recurrent (quasi-periodic) orbits their error in first integrals stays bounded, while a non-symmetric method such as RK4 accumulates a secular drift; on an escaping geodesic nothing recurs and the local speed errors can saturate for any method (on the vertical hyperbolic ray the right-hand side is linear along the ray, so every Runge-Kutta method keeps the speed).
numerical_result: RK4 error exponent 4.941 (measured/predicted 0.901-1.02); required steps for k = 1, 2, 4, 8: RK4 23, 54, 127, 303 (exponent 1.24), implicit midpoint 832, 2311, 6532, 18476 (exponent 1.49), 2-stage Gauss-Legendre 15, 35, 83, 196 (exponent 1.24, 0.647 to 0.654 times the RK4 steps, predicted (120/720)^(1/4) = 0.639), DP45 81, 162, 300, 505 (exponent 0.881); accuracy/stability step ratio 23-50.5; growth and decay rates of the integrated Phi(L) equal k to 1.6e-11 and 6.3e-11 relative (decay resolvable for k <= 4); RK4 geodesic endpoint error 2.2e-09 (k = 1) to 0.461 (k = 8); implicit midpoint at kh = 2.29 changes sign 6 times; saddle j_head(L) 3.168, 14.26, 105.8, 793.8, 5775, 4.136e+04, 2.946e+05, 2.094e+06 for c = 1, 4, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096, 16384 (fitted exponent 1.43 for c >= 16, local exponents 1.454, 1.431, 1.42, 1.416, 1.415 from c = 16), DP45 steps grow by 47, 52, 48, 48, 47, 46, 46 per factor 4 in c. Full nonlinear systems: Gauss-Legendre j_head orders 4, 4, 4.001, 4.002 (RK4 3.986, 3.972, 3.944, 3.888) for k = 1, 2, 4, 8, GL/RK4 j_head error at N = 256 0.1677, 0.1689, 0.1711, 0.1756 (1/6 = 0.1667), equal to its step-matrix power to 4.4e-14, relative error at the step-matrix counts 15, 35, 83, 196 up to 9.872e-07 and one step below at least 1.007e-06; hyperbolic end-point error ratio GL/RK4 0.704-1.28 and speed error ratio 0.695-1.06 (k <= 4); saddle j_head orders 3.93-4.147, GL/RK4 j_head error ratios c = 1 ridge 0.826, c = 1 oblique 1.32, c = 4 ridge 0.359, c = 4 oblique 0.301, c = 16 ridge 0.274, c = 16 oblique 2.45, GL/RK4 speed error ratio at most 0.207; fixed-point iterations per step 5-14.9 (hyperbolic plane) and 4.75-9.41 (saddle) for Gauss-Legendre; winding torus speed-error envelope at L = 160 over L = 20: RK4 10.5 (last local slope 1.07), implicit midpoint 1.0001, Gauss-Legendre 1.00004 (9.26 and 11.1 iterations per step); on the escaping geodesics every envelope ratio is at most 1.007, and the vertical hyperbolic ray keeps the speed to 2.2e-15 for every method; implicit midpoint on the full HyperbolicPlane(8) system at kh = 2.29: refused ('implicit-midpoint stage equations did not converge within 60 fixed-point iterations at step size 0.2857142857142857 (step 1 of 7)').
observation_model: Relative error of j_head(L); required steps by doubling and bisection on the exact step matrices of RK4, implicit midpoint and 2-stage Gauss-Legendre (matrix powers, checked against the scalar stability function on the eigenmodes, and for RK4 against the full geodesic/Jacobi integration); hyperbolic distance of the geodesic endpoint to the exact semicircle; for the full nonlinear comparison the j_head and end-point errors against the closed forms (hyperbolic plane) or the DP45 reference (saddle; errors below 1e-11 are not fitted), and the running maximum of |g(v, v) - 1| along each run (speed-error envelope).

title: Study stiff behavior on strongly negative-curvature surfaces.
uncertainty: Step counts are integers found by bisection assuming monotone error in N; the saddle local exponents (1.454, 1.431, 1.42, 1.416, 1.415 for c = 16 ... 16384) come from adaptive runs self-consistent to 3.5e-09 relative, so each local exponent is accurate to about 1e-8; the sqrt(2) limit is a matched-asymptotics argument supported by these slopes, not a proof. The nonlinear Gauss-Legendre results carry the stage-solve residual (tolerance 1e-13) and rounding. Where a fixed-point iteration stops can change by one iteration between platforms (it did for one step in 640 between OpenBLAS kernels), which moves a Gauss-Legendre state by up to about 1e-14 relative: up to 1e-3 of the smallest errors used (1e-11), so orders and error ratios built from them are compared within 1e-3 to 5e-3, while the speed envelopes (1e-6 and larger) move by less than 1e-8 relative.
unresolved_assumptions: The sqrt(2) saddle exponent is a matched-asymptotics argument, not a proof
The sqrt(2) exponent is fitted on the ridge geodesic only; oblique saddle geodesics are compared for integrator accuracy, not for their Jacobi growth law

The nonlinear implicit integrator solves its stage equations by fixed-point iteration, which within its 60-iteration cap reaches only kh below about 0.6 (implicit midpoint) and 1.1 (Gauss-Legendre) here (without the cap it stops converging near kh = 1 and 1.3); a Newton solve would reach larger steps and is not implemented
Why the Gauss-Legendre/RK4 error ratio varies between saddle geodesics is measured, not derived from the methods' error expansions
Error amplification of the geodesic in the half-plane chart mixes chart compression near y = 0 with intrinsic instability
